newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola hits new lows on bright crop prospects.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola hits new lows on bright crop prospects.

text.p: WCE canola futures were lower at midsession and new contract lows were set on bright crop prospects in Canada and in the U.S. which were trimming any urgency to hold on to nearby stocks, traders said.
"The crop looks pretty good up here and everybody is bearish," a trader said.
The new low for July is $384.00 per tonne, below the previous low of $384.10. At 1205 CDT canola was unchanged to $0.70 lower with July down $0.60 at $385.10 a tonne.
Traders said the deferred contracts were holding up better than the nearbys.
"They're not quite as bearish in the back end. There's a Stats Canada report out tomorrow and there might not be quite as many acres," the trader said.
New contract lows were set in feed wheat. The new low for July is $149.50, below the previous low of $150.50. Feed wheat was unchanged to $1.00 lower with July down $1.00 at $149.50.
New lows also were set in western barley. The new low for July is $124.50, below the previous low of $125.00.
Oats were US$0.20 to US$1.00 lower, with July down US$1.00 at US$113.00.
Flax was $1.30 to $3.30 lower with July down $1.30 at $328.70.
Feed peas were unchanged to $0.50 up with July unchanged at $173.50.
(All prices in Canadian dollars per tonne except feedpeas and oats.)
